title: Greek village salad (horiatiki)
summary: Chunks of tomato, cucumber, green pepper and red onion with olives, oregano and good olive oil, topped with a slab of feta.
steps: Put the tomato, cucumber, green pepper, onion and olives in a wide, shallow bowl and sprinkle with the salt. Leave 5 minutes so the tomatoes release a little juice.
Pour over the olive oil and vinegar and toss gently.
Lay the feta on top in one piece, sprinkle the oregano over it, and drizzle with a little more oil. Break the feta up at the table.

swaps.note: leave out the feta, add about 100 g more olives and an extra 2 tbsp olive oil

dairy_free_notes: Without feta the salad loses its salty, creamy centre; extra olives and oil keep it rich and briny, but it is a different, lighter salad.
tips: Don't refrigerate the tomatoes; cold dulls their flavour.

origin.history: Horiatiki, 'village salad', combines vegetables that have long been eaten across Greece, but as a fixed dish with a slab of feta it seems to have become popular in Greek tavernas in the mid-twentieth century. It spread worldwide with tourism from the 1960s and 1970s. Traditional versions contain no lettuce.
